🚀 Bay Area Speech AI for Healthcare & Education Workshop @ UC Berkeley We’re excited to announce that Berkeley Speech Group will be hosting the first Bay Area Speech AI for Healthcare and Education Workshop at UC Berkeley on November 21st, 12:00PM–7 PM! This event brings together researchers, clinicians, and technologists to share state-of-the-art progress in Speech AI — including our own group’s latest breakthroughs across multiple dimensions — and to discuss the future of AI-powered healthcare and education. In partnership with UCSF Multitudes , we’ll also showcase our latest AI-supported demo for children’s language screening, developed to support California’s universal K-2 language screening initiative. 🔬 Keynote & Highlights Gopala Krishna Anumanchipalli and I’ll be giving a keynote talk on the latest advances in speech and language disorders, bridging AI research, healthcare, and education, with a look at where we are now — and where the field is heading. We’ll also present ongoing research across several major directions: 1. Universal AI Battery for Kids’ Language Function — Modular AI for scalable, automated K-2 language screening integrated with UCSF Multitudes. 2. Dysfluency Modeling — A general AI framework for speech-language disorders, and its clinical translation to Primary Progressive Aphasia 3. Modern AI Solutions for Dyslexia 4. Modern AI Solutions for Semantic Variant Primary Progressive Aphasia (svPPA) 5. Universal Articulatory Speech Language Disorder Analysis 6. Foundation AI Models for Speech Healthcare: 6.1 Universal Phonetic Encoder 6.2 Speech Generation as Articulatory Robot Planning 6.3 Automatic Long-Form Disordered Speech Processing 7. Agentic AI for Speech Language Disorders 8. Universal Language Screening Product Showcase 🔗 More info: https://lnkd.in/gDbuQxXt 📩 Interested in joining (in-person or online)? If you’re at Berkeley or beyond, either major in or just interested in speech AI for healthcare and education, or discuss future collaborations. Please attend it! Feel free to DM me or fill out the interest form ( https://lnkd.in/g2nMKGt3 ). Attendance is by invitation only. Location is TBD. We also welcome external speakers to contribute talks at this workshop, alongside our internal presentations. Please feel free to contact me if you’re interested in participating. Credit to all amazing organizers Celine Chen Maggie Dong Anaisha Das Rohit Mekkoth Chenxu Guo Harrison Li Cathy Sheng Sarika Pasumarthy Sanjana Taware Minggang Li Saaketh Kanduri Ayush Ghosh Akshay Anand #Speech #Healthcare #Education #AIHealth ...more ...more

Have you ever started reading a research paper and realized you could barely comprehend the abstract? As one of the top three finalists in the Creativity Track at the UC Berkeley AI Hackathon 2025, myself, Evan Chisholm , Sai Rithvik Kotla , Chakshan Kothakota , and Dimple Amitha Garuadapuri tried to address this issue. We believe that oftentimes there is a comprehension barrier in academic research papers that are not generally written to explain something to a novice. As student researchers, we understood the feeling of being unable to make it past the abstract when trying to understand a complex paper. We wanted to change that, making research more accessible and providing different avenues of understanding. This is where the idea for README AI came from. Watch, understand, implement - research made accessible README AI takes in a research paper and… - Creates a clean tailored explainer video with a voice-over (akin to 3Blue1Brown or Khan Academy Videos) with targeted and accurate animations grounded in the research paper you’re trying to understand - Highlights key concepts of the paper with text citations on a web interface - Generates a quiz for users to test their understanding of the concepts from the paper - Hosts a library of your analyzed papers and educational videos to reference past materials You can check out our work here!: https://lnkd.in/gkcBmG4W Huge thank you to the CalHacks team for hosting this amazing event. I had an incredible time meeting and collaborating with my teammates over the course of 24 hours to bring a tool that I would use on a daily basis to life. Our next step is to make this available to students. If you’re interested in what we're creating or passionate about accessible EdTech, we would love to hear from you! ...more

Last week, I wrapped up my 12-week Summer 2026 internship at Amazon! This summer, I worked on the Post-Silicon Validation & Bringup team for Amazon Leo , where I designed and built a generic, data-driven serial C2C communication protocol test engine on an STM32 microcontroller, helping validate our modem ASIC's communication capabilities. Building the system gave me the chance to work across embedded firmware, low-level debugging, hardware bringup, and post-silicon validation. I spent a lot of time working through race conditions, timing, and latency issues, tackling signal integrity and power integrity, and thinking through architectural tradeoffs around how to keep firmware scalable and maintainable. After seeing firsthand the challenges of hardware reliability and validation, I'm proud to have built a solution that makes testing more scalable, repeatable, and efficient across PVT corners. I'm also incredibly proud to have contributed, even in a small way, to Amazon Leo's mission to expand access to fast, reliable internet. Reliable connectivity is still out of reach for many people, businesses, and communities around the world, so working alongside engineers building a low-Earth-orbit satellite network to help close that gap made the experience especially meaningful. None of this would have been possible without the people who supported me throughout the summer. Thank you to my manager Prasaanthan Yoganathan , my mentor Jimit Patel , my onboarding buddy Morgan Pothoff , and everyone else on the team for the time, patience, technical guidance, feedback, and encouragement you gave me along the way.

Back at Unit 1, where I lived as a first-year, to participate in an opinionated discussion aptly titled “What Really Matters” to this year’s CS Kickstart program with Stella Kaval and Mallika Reddy . CS Kickstart has changed my professional trajectory in so many ways: from majoring in computer science, to starting research at Cal (thanks Jennifer Grannen :D), publishing our first poster with the hopes of meeting THE Professor Colleen Lewis , and getting guidance from so many people who helped me navigate applying to grad school (including our great advisor Audrey Raya Sillers ). Most importantly, the program introduced me to Mallika and Stella. Obligatory friend brag: one started med school this week, and the other has now hit a year of killing it at Meta. Our final message to first-years was short and sweet: Invest in the people you want to grow with. And try to remember that there is no such thing as a “best path.” Shoutout to the lead directors Emma Lee , Jaclyn Huynh , Hanna Tran and all of leadership and the volunteers this yr. I think a large reason CSK "works" is because it is student-led. Check out the program and consider contributing to its future: https://lnkd.in/ge5mkPgZ

Honored to share that I received the Dean's Prize for Excellence in Research from UCLA's Division of Life Sciences for my work on ATAD2 Inhibition as a Strategy Against Advanced Breast Cancer! This research is part of my ongoing senior honors thesis in Dr. Tanya Stoyanova's lab at UCLA, where I'm investigating ATAD2 as a therapeutic target for advanced and treatment-resistant breast cancers. Still very much a work in progress, and I couldn't be more excited about where it's headed. This year I had the privilege of presenting my work at multiple conferences, including the LABEST conference, UCLA’s Undergraduate Research Week, and the MCDB Research Poster Session, with each experience pushing me to communicate my work more clearly and connect with other researchers. Thank you to Dr. Tanya Stoyanova , my mentor Diana Argiles Castillo , and everyone who has supported my journey this far!

So pleased to share that Opal Therapeutics has been awarded a $1.25 million SBIR Phase II award from the National Science Foundation (NSF) to accelerate the future of women's health drug discovery 🙋🏽‍♀️ . 🧪 Women’s health has entered a new era driven by deep science, enabling technologies, and a growing recognition of the tremendous commercial opportunity in developing better therapies for conditions such as endometriosis and uterine fibroids. Our patient-derived "uterus-in-a-dish" platform enables pharmaceutical and biotech companies to evaluate therapeutics directly in human uterine tissue models, helping identify the right drug candidates earlier and reduce reliance on animal models. The NSF award allows us to expand our infrastructure and meet the growing demands of our and biotech/pharma partners. ✏️ See the full award details in our press release here: https://lnkd.in/gjF7nNfp I'm incredibly grateful to our team and advisors to get to this point. Amber Cramer , Aabid Shariff, Jennifer Madrigal , Arpitha Rao , Anika Mittal , Carolyn Kreuzkamp , Jean-Charles NEEL #endometriosis #fibroids #nsf #womenshealth #drugdiscovery

Meet Sarah Goody and Viplove Rahate , two gifted UC Berkeley students I’m happy to host this Wednesday at SHACK15 . Sarah founded the youth-led Climate NOW at just 14-years-old. She’s become a national a voice on climate issues and concussions. Profiled by Good Morning America, CNN and NBC, she’s written for Teen Vogue and Business Insider. We connected because we both got our start at the Redwood High Bark paper. Sarah received the Princess Diana Award in 2020, the highest honor for youth philanthropic efforts. Viplove and I met at Shack15. He’s a young, smart engineer with a curious mindset. He’s interning at Google on the Agent Monetization team. This fall he’ll intern at Tesla’s Vehicle Software team. He’s excited about “building things people actually use.” Sarah is majoring in legal studies with a minor in public policy, while Viplove is studying Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Industrial Engineering and Operations Research. Meet Sarah and Viplove at the Shack15 Community Tea this Wednesday, August 5 at 3pm. Two talented University of California, Berkeley students already making waves out in the world. They’ve never met., and I’m thrilled to bring them to meet my pals & colleagues for inspiring conversations. See you Wednesday!
